x.A: Multi-AZ replicates writes synchronously to a standby in another AZ, so committed transactions are not lost on failover. It gives an RPO close to zero, under a second.

x.C: Read replicas replicate asynchronously, so there can be lag and data could be lost, so the RPO isn't under a second.
x.D: A DMS CDC task has replication latency and isn't a synchronous copy, and the database stays in one AZ.

x.C: Putting instances in public subnets with Elastic IPs exposes them directly to the internet.
x.D: Allowing any TCP traffic on any port on the ALB's security group makes the ALB more open and doesn't restrict the instances.
